## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷantaraduka* ("Shorter Intermediate Set of Dyads") constitutes section 2.2 of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka. Within the Abhidhamma mātikā, the dyad matrix consists of one hundred couplets organized into thirteen groups: ten corruption clusters (*gocchaka*) and three miscellaneous intermediate or supplementary divisions, namely the *cūḷantaraduka* (a short series of seven couplets), the *mahantaraduka* (fourteen couplets), and the *piṭṭhiduka* (eighteen couplets) [Potter, Abhidharma Buddhism]. Modern scholars observe that these intermediate groups appear to represent an older stratum of the matrix [Potter, Abhidharma Buddhism]. Several dyads in the *cūḷantaraduka* feature strict grammatical negations and polar classifications, such as *sappaccaya* / *appaccaya* (states conditioned by causes vs. not conditioned by causes) and *saṅkhata* / *asaṅkhata* (conditioned vs. unconditioned) [Watanabe 1983; Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics]. In these couplets, the positive member encompasses the five aggregates (*khandha*s), whereas the negative counterpart isolates the unconditioned element (*nibbāna*) [Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics].

 Within the *Paṭṭhāna*, the text's conditional exposition shares its longest formulaic segments with adjacent dyad and triplet divisions, most prominently the *Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 2.10), *Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 2.13), *Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 2.1), and *Kusalattika* (Patthana 1.2) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus generates cross-language alignments with northern scholastic treatises, aligning segments with Sanskrit works such as Vasubandhu’s *Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇa*, Harivarman’s *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, and the *Mahāvyutpatti*, as well as Tibetan translations of the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, *Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā*, and the *Yogācārabhūmi* [DharmaNexus].
